Les langues officielles du Canada sont le français et l’anglais. Les personnes qui peuvent parler les deux langues sont désignées comme bilingues. Selon le Recensement de la population de 2021, environ 4,2 millions de Canadiens (12,3 %) pouvaient parler les deux langues officielles du Canada, ce qui représente une augmentation de 16,7 % depuis 2016. La proportion de Canadiens bilingues a augmenté de 0,8 point de pourcentage depuis 2016. L’anglais est la langue maternelle ou la langue d’usage à la maison d’une plus grande proportion de la population que le français, et les deux langues officielles sont parlées par une plus grande proportion de la population que l’une ou l’autre langue officielle seule. Toutefois, dans les provinces et territoires hors Québec, la proportion de la population qui parle le français (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison) est plus élevée que la proportion de la population qui parle l’anglais et le français (bilingues). Au Québec, la proportion de la population qui parle le français (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison) est plus élevée que la proportion de la population qui parle l’anglais et le français (bilingues) ou qui parle l’anglais (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison). La proportion de la population bilingue est la plus élevée au Québec et au Nouveau-Brunswick. Au Nouveau-Brunswick, la proportion de la population bilingue est plus élevée que la proportion de la population qui parle l’anglais (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison). La proportion de la population bilingue est la plus faible en Saskatchewan et en Alberta. En Saskatchewan, la proportion de la population bilingue est inférieure à la proportion de la population qui parle le français (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison) et à la proportion de la population qui parle l’anglais (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison). En Alberta, la proportion de la population bilingue est inférieure à la proportion de la population qui parle l’anglais (langue maternelle ou langue d’usage à la maison). Le français est la langue d’usage à la maison d’une plus grande proportion de la population au Québec que dans les autres provinces et territoires. L’anglais est la langue d’usage à la maison d’une plus grande proportion de la population dans les autres provinces et territoires que dans la province de Québec. Note aux lecteurs

Elle ne s'applique pas non plus aux personnes qui travaillent dans un domaine de compétence provinciale. La Loi sur les relations de travail au Manitoba et la Loi sur les accidents de travail régissent le travail dans les secteurs de compétence provinciale, et la Loi sur l'indemnité de congé annuel s'applique aux employés du secteur privé. Lorsque vous quittez la Saskatchewan pour étudier ailleurs au Canada, vous devez vous assurer de maintenir votre résidence en Saskatchewan afin de demeurer admissible aux services de santé financés par l'État, y compris le Programme de médicaments sur ordonnance et le programme de prestations dentaires. Cela signifie que vous devez avoir l'intention de retourner vivre en Saskatchewan et y avoir maintenu votre résidence principale. Pour vérifier que vous êtes admissible, vous devez vous assurer de répondre à tous les critères suivants :
- Vous devez avoir un permis de conduire valide de la Saskatchewan ou un autre document d'identité officiel qui prouve que vous êtes résident de la Saskatchewan.
- Vous devez avoir maintenu votre résidence principale en Saskatchewan, ce qui signifie que vous devez avoir maintenu votre adresse en Saskatchewan et y avoir payé vos impôts sur le revenu.
- Vous devez avoir maintenu votre statut de résident permanent de la Saskatchewan, ce qui signifie que vous devez avoir maintenu votre statut de résident permanent de la province et y avoir payé vos impôts sur le revenu.
Si vous ne répondez pas à ces critères, vous pourriez être considéré comme un résident temporaire et vous pourriez ne pas être admissible aux services de santé financés par l'État de la Saskatchewan. Il est donc important de vous assurer de répondre à tous ces critères pour maintenir votre admissibilité.

You are considered a resident of Canada for income tax purposes if you establish significant residential ties with Canada. You usually establish these ties by living in Canada for 183 days or more in a calendar year. You also usually establish these ties if you have a dwelling in Canada (or you own one) and, if you or your spouse or common-law partner have recently immigrated to Canada, you continue to own and maintain a dwelling in your former country. If you are considered a resident of Canada for income tax purposes, you have to report your worldwide income on your Canadian income tax and benefit return. If you have been working in Canada, you may want to ask your employer for a T4, Statement of Remuneration Paid. The amounts on this form can help you when you complete your Canadian income tax and benefit return. Do I need a social insurance number? If you are a resident of Canada, you will need a social insurance number (SIN) to work in Canada or to receive benefits and services from the government. If you are a temporary resident, you can apply for a SIN only if you have a work permit or study permit. Do I need a Canadian bank account? You do not need a Canadian bank account to file your income tax and benefit return. However, if you have a balance owing, you must pay your balance by April 30 of the year following the tax year. If you have a balance owing and you are unable to pay in full, you should make your best effort to pay as much as you can by the April 30 payment deadline. This will avoid interest charges. You have to report your worldwide income on your Canadian income tax and benefit return, unless you are considered a factual resident of Canada. If you are considered a factual resident of Canada, you only have to report your worldwide income for the part of the year that you were resident in Canada for income tax purposes. If you are considered a resident of Canada for income tax purposes, you can authorize a person or agency to be your representative for income tax purposes. Your representative can be a family member, a friend, or a paid representative, such as a tax preparation service. Your representative can be granted authorization in a limited capacity, such as just to communicate with the CRA, or in a full capacity, such as to represent you in all your dealings with the CRA. The subscriber is responsible for making the EAP payment to the beneficiary, who is the student or individual who will use the funds for their education expenses. 3. You want to know the maximum amounts for the EAP and the refund of contributions. The maximum amount for the EAP is determined by the RESP's contribution limits and the beneficiary's education expenses. The maximum amount for the refund of contributions is also determined by the RESP's contribution limits. 4. You want to know what the refund of contributions is used for. The refund of contributions is used to pay for education expenses, such as tuition, books, and living expenses. It can also be used to pay off student loans or other education-related debts. 5. You want to know how contributions and EAPs are taxed. Contributions to an RESP are not tax-deductible, but the income earned on the contributions is tax-exempt until the funds are withdrawn. The income earned on an RESP is tax-exempt until the funds are withdrawn. When the funds are withdrawn, the income is taxed in the hands of the beneficiary. - **La fête nationale du Québec** :
	Cette fête est célébrée en l'honneur de la naissance de la nation québécoise, qui a été officiellement établie le 24 juin 1867. Elle est une occasion pour les Québécois de célébrer leur identité, leur culture et leur histoire.

- **La fête du Canada** :
	Cette fête est célébrée pour commémorer l'union des provinces canadiennes en une seule nation, qui a eu lieu le 1er juillet 1867. Elle est une occasion pour les Canadiens de célébrer leur identité nationale, leur diversité et leur unité.

Pour distinguer ces deux fêtes, il est important de les présenter comme des événements distincts, avec leurs propres symboles, traditions et significations. However, the employee will still receive their holiday pay entitlement. The holiday pay entitlement is calculated based on the previous year's earnings. The holiday pay entitlement must be paid no later than the pay day closest to December 1. The holiday pay entitlement is calculated by adding up the employee's earnings for the 4-week period immediately before the general holiday and dividing that total by 20. The resulting amount is the holiday pay entitlement for the general holiday. For example, if an employee earns $1,000 in the 4-week period before a general holiday, their holiday pay entitlement would be $50 ($1,000 ÷ 20 = $50). La formation professionnelle

Les centres de formation professionnelle (CFP) et les écoles des métiers, les collèges d'enseignement général et professionnel (cégep) et les universités assurent la formation professionnelle au Québec. Les CFP et les écoles des métiers offrent une formation technique de courte durée qui mène à l'obtention d'un diplôme d'études professionnelles (DEP) ou d'une attestation de spécialisation professionnelle (ASP). Les programmes de formation peuvent être de courte ou de longue durée. Les programmes de courte durée mènent à l'obtention d'un DEP et durent généralement entre 600 et 1 800 heures. Les programmes de longue durée mènent à l'obtention d'un DEP et d'une ASP et durent généralement entre 1 800 et 2 400 heures. Pour être admis à un programme de formation, vous devez avoir réussi les cours de niveau secondaire requis, notamment la langue d'enseignement au Québec, la langue seconde et les mathématiques. La formation est subventionnée par le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Formation professionnelle du Québec. Les frais de scolarité sont de 150 $ par année scolaire. Les frais pour l'obtention du diplôme et les frais de subsistance sont à la charge de l'étudiant.

Why does a Quebec calendar call the May Monday holiday Journée nationale des patriotes while a calendar elsewhere in Canada calls that date Victoria Day? While it is Monday, May 20, 2019 for everyone in Canada, this date is known as Victoria Day in most of Canada and Journée nationale des patriotes in Quebec. You can check the name of this holiday on the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages’ calendar tool. The reasons for this difference are historical. On the one hand, the sovereign’s birthday has been celebrated in Canada since the reign of Queen Victoria, who ruled over the United Kingdom, Canada and several other countries. The sovereign’s birthday was officially named Victoria Day in 1953. On the other hand, Quebec’s National Assembly designated the Monday before May 25 as Journée nationale des patriotes in 2003. This date commemorates the struggle and sacrifices of the patriots during the 1837-1838 rebellion. In short, these two holidays are not synonymous. You can consult the list of holidays in Canada to learn more. This article was written in collaboration with the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages. You may think that when the Bank of Canada lowers or raises its policy interest rate, it affects all borrowing rates equally. You would be right - and you would be wrong. Whether you realize it or not, changes in the Bank of Canada’s policy interest rate have different effects on different borrowing rates over time. Understanding how these changes work can help you manage debt during periods of high and low interest rates. Three interest rates you should know about

There are three interest rates that are important when it comes to household borrowing:

The target for the overnight rate. This is the rate that the Bank of Canada says should be the actual rate at which major banks lend and borrow from one another one-day (or overnight) funds. The target rate is announced by the Bank of Canada eight times a year. It is the basis for other interest rates, including mortgage rates. The prime rate. The prime rate is a rate that banks charge other banks or their most creditworthy business customers. It is influenced by the target rate and is usually the same among major banks in Canada. The prime rate is used to determine variable mortgage rates. Fixed mortgage rates. Fixed mortgage rates are determined by longer-term funding sources and by the demand for five-year mortgage rates. Fixed mortgage rates are not directly affected by changes in the target rate. How the target rate and the prime rate affect your variable mortgage rate

A change in the target rate is the single most important factor for changes in the prime rate. If the target rate rises, the prime rate will also rise. This is true for a decrease in the target rate as well. For example, if the target rate rises by 0.50 of a percentage point from 4.25% to 4.75%, the prime rate will likely rise by the same amount, which means you will pay more in interest on a variable mortgage. This change will take effect right away and will add to your monthly mortgage payment. You can expect changes in the prime rate to be passed on to you by your lender within one to four business days, depending on the lender in question. Most lenders offer a grace period on variable-rate mortgages. This means the increase in your mortgage payment will not take effect for one or two months after your lender has passed on the increase. However, variable-rate mortgages can be renewed at any time, so you may face higher interest costs even during your current term. How the prime rate affects your home equity line of credit

The prime rate also determines the interest you pay on a home equity line of credit. If your home equity line of credit is linked to the prime rate, the lender will charge you interest based on the prime rate charge by your lender. Any increase or decrease in the prime rate will affect the interest you pay. Fixed-rate home equity lines of credit are also available so that you can lock in your interest rate for a fixed period. The interest rate on a fixed-rate home equity line of credit is typically higher than on a variable-rate home equity line of credit because you are protected against a rise in interest rates. The spread between a fixed rate and a variable rate reflects the interest rate outlook for the term as well as the costs of insuring the lender from a rate increase. The prime rate and your credit card interest rate

Most credit cards offered by banks and other financial institutions have a variable interest rate that is affected by changes in the prime rate. You will pay more in interest on a credit card if the prime rate climbs. However, there is a delay before your credit card interest rate will be affected. In addition, if you have a variable interest rate on your credit card, even a small rate increase may impact you because the compound interest effect is working against you. To reduce your costs if the prime rate rises, try to make payments against your credit card balance that are larger than the minimum amount owing. With some lenders, you can choose a fixed-rate credit card. This may protect you against an increase in interest rates for a fixed term, but you must consider the total cost of the loan, including any balance that will remain at the end of the term. A fixed interest rate may be higher than the variable interest rate. The prime rate and your saving rate

Changes in the target rate also affect the interest you earn on your savings. If the target rate rises, your bank may start paying you a higher interest rate on your savings. However, banks usually increase their saving rates more slowly than the increase in the target rate. Your deposit protection

It is important to remember that interest rates affect the value of investments such as Guaranteed Investment Certificates (GICs) and bank term deposits. By knowing the type of investments you have, you will be able to manage your risks. As an investor, you have two key concerns when it comes to your deposits: to receive the interest on your investments and to get your money back when the term ends. Quels sont les principaux produits livrables pour une évaluation d’impact? La publication de l’évaluation d’impact dans la Gazette du Canada est le produit livrable final et un jalon clé dans le processus d’évaluation d’impact. Vous trouverez de plus amples renseignements sur les produits livrables dans la Directive du Cabinet sur l’évaluation environnementale des projets de politiques, de plans et de programmes. Quels sont les différents types d’évaluation d’impact? Un processus d’évaluation d’impact peut être mené de deux façons différentes, soit comme une évaluation d’impact stratégique (EIS) ou comme une évaluation d’impact (EA). Une EIS est menée au début d’un projet, avant que des décisions clés soient prises. Une EA est menée au moment où un projet est élaboré. Qu’est-ce qu’une évaluation d’impact stratégique (EIS)? Une EIS est un type d’évaluation d’impact mené au début d’un projet, avant que des décisions clés soient prises. Une EIS est axée sur l’examen des grands enjeux et des solutions de rechange stratégiques, y compris les politiques et les plans de rechange, en vue d’éclairer les décisions préliminaires. Les évaluations stratégiques sont moins détaillées et ne portent pas sur les détails du projet. Elles sont utilisées pour faire avancer les projets avant que des décisions clés ne soient prises. Qu’est-ce qu’une évaluation d’impact (EA)? Une EA est un type d’évaluation d’impact menée au moment où un projet est élaboré. Elle examine les effets environnementaux potentiels du projet et des solutions de rechange. Une EA fournit des renseignements utiles pour la prise de décisions à l’étape de l’élaboration du projet. Elle est axée sur les détails du projet et son contenu est plus précis que celui d’une évaluation stratégique. Quels sont les effets environnementaux examinés dans le cadre d’une évaluation d’impact? Les effets environnementaux sont les changements que peuvent entraîner un projet dans l’environnement, y compris les effets sur la santé et les écosystèmes. Les effets environnementaux sont évalués à l’aide des facteurs prescrits par la Loi sur l’évaluation d’impact. Ces facteurs comprennent les changements qui peuvent survenir dans les domaines suivants : la qualité de l’air, la qualité de l’eau, la quantité d’eau, la faune et la flore, la santé humaine et la santé des écosystèmes. Qu’est-ce qu’une déclaration publique d’intérêt? Une déclaration publique d’intérêt (DPI) est un processus qui permet aux personnes intéressées de signaler leur désir de participer au processus d’évaluation d’impact d’un projet. Il s’agit d’une occasion pour les personnes intéressées de faire connaître leur intérêt à participer à l’évaluation d’impact d’un projet. Les personnes qui présentent une DPI sont ensuite tenues informées du processus d’évaluation d’impact du projet et peuvent participer à ce processus. The process of initiating a proposal for federal public spending in Parliament involves several steps and requires the participation of various actors. You are here because you want to know who can initiate a proposal for federal public spending in Parliament and in which chamber the spending bill must start. The answer to this question is as follows:

The process of initiating a proposal for federal public spending in Parliament begins with the executive branch, which is responsible for proposing the budget and presenting it to Parliament. The budget is then reviewed and debated in Parliament, and amendments may be proposed by members of Parliament. The final budget is then approved by Parliament and becomes law.

In terms of the specific actors involved, the executive branch, which includes the President and the government, is responsible for proposing the budget. Members of Parliament, who are elected by the people, are responsible for reviewing and debating the budget, and proposing amendments. The final decision on the budget is made by Parliament as a whole.

In terms of the specific chamber, the process of initiating a proposal for federal public spending in Parliament typically begins in the lower house of Parliament, which is the House of Commons in Canada. The budget is then debated and amended in the House of Commons, and then sent to the upper house, which is the Senate, for further review and approval.

It is worth noting that the process of initiating a proposal for federal public spending in Parliament can vary depending on the country and its specific system of government. However, in general, the process involves the executive branch proposing the budget, Parliament reviewing and debating the budget, and ultimately approving it.

You may have heard the expression, “the power of the purse.” That phrase reminds us that the British North America Act of 1867 gives Parliament the power to tax and spend, and that the Executive, represented by the Government, needs Parliament’s approval to spend money. You may also have heard that a budget vote is considered a “confidence” matter. That means that if the House of Commons votes against the budget, the Government has lost the confidence of the House, and the Government is expected to resign. In British Columbia, the provincial budget vote is also a confidence matter. In fact, section 25 of the Constitution Act, 1867 says that “It shall not be lawful for the House of Commons to adopt or pass any Vote, Resolution, Address, or Bill for the Appropriation of any Part of the Public Revenue, or of any Tax or Impost, to any Purpose that has not been first recommended to that House by Message of the Governor General in the Session in which such Vote, Resolution, Address, or Bill is proposed.” The message from the Governor General is called a “royal recommendation.” It is an indication that the Governor General has been consulted about the budget, and that the Governor General has agreed to the budget. The royal recommendation is required for all budget bills, including the main estimates, the supplementary estimates, and the budget bill itself. If the House of Commons votes against the budget, the Government is expected to resign. This is because the Government has lost the confidence of the House, and the Government is no longer able to govern. You should consider the following factors when deciding whether a data breach poses a real risk of significant harm under PIPEDA:

- **Type of information**: The type of information involved in the breach, such as sensitive personal information, financial data, or health information.

- **Sensitivity of the information**: The sensitivity of the information involved, such as if it is easily accessible or if it requires a high level of security clearance.

- **Impact on individuals**: The impact of the breach on individuals, such as financial loss, identity theft, or reputational damage.

- **Number of affected individuals**: The number of individuals affected by the breach, as this can increase the likelihood of significant harm.

- **Extent of the breach**: The extent of the breach, such as if it is limited to a small group of individuals or if it involves a large number of people.

- **Duration of the breach**: The duration of the breach, such as if it was a one-time event or if it was ongoing.

- **Actions taken to mitigate the breach**: The actions taken by the organization to mitigate the breach, such as notifying affected individuals, implementing security measures, or providing support to those affected.

- **Previous breaches**: The organization's history of breaches, as this can indicate a pattern of negligence or a lack of security measures.

- **Industry standards**: Industry standards and best practices for data security, such as compliance with regulatory requirements or adherence to industry guidelines.

By considering these factors, organizations can make an informed decision about whether a data breach poses a real risk of significant harm under PIPEDA and take appropriate action to mitigate the breach and protect individuals. You can find more information on data breaches and how to report them on the official website of the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.

La question est de savoir si un nid d’oiseau migrateur peut être enlevé lorsqu’il n’y a plus d’œufs ni d’oisillons à l’intérieur, mais qu’il s’agit toujours d’une espèce migratrice. Vous savez peut-être que les nids de certaines espèces d’oiseaux migrateurs peuvent être enlevés sans autorisation, à condition que l’on s’assure qu’il ne reste aucun œuf ou oisillon à l’intérieur du nid. Le cas particulier du nid d’oiseau migrateur est un bon exemple de la complexité de la réglementation environnementale canadienne. La Loi sur la protection des espèces en péril (LPEP) et la Loi sur les espèces sauvages du Canada (LESWC) sont les deux lois principales qui régissent la protection des espèces sauvages au Canada. La LPEP vise à protéger les espèces en péril, tandis que la LESWC réglemente la chasse, la pêche et la récolte des espèces sauvages. Les deux lois ont des exigences spécifiques pour la protection des nids d’oiseaux migrateurs. Selon la LPEP, il est interdit de détruire, de mutiler ou de retirer un nid d’oiseau migrateur, même si l’espèce n’est pas en péril. Dans le cadre du processus de négociation de traités de la Colombie-Britannique, le gouvernement du Canada, le gouvernement de la Colombie-Britannique et les Premières Nations s’engagent à négocier des traités globaux, mais les Premières Nations ont la possibilité de négocier des ententes progressives, aussi appelées ententes de type « traités ». Ces ententes progressives sont négociées au cas par cas et sont fondées sur les besoins et les intérêts uniques de chaque Première Nation. Les ententes progressives peuvent inclure des dispositions telles que des accords de cogestion, des accords de partage des revenus, des accords de développement économique et des accords de protection de l’environnement. Les ententes progressives peuvent être négociées en même temps qu’un traité global, mais elles ne sont pas obligatoires et ne sont pas incluses dans le traité global. Les ententes progressives sont un outil important pour les Premières Nations qui souhaitent avancer dans la négociation de traités globaux, mais qui ont besoin de solutions plus rapides et plus ciblées pour répondre à leurs besoins uniques. Elles permettent aux Premières Nations de prendre le contrôle de leur propre destin et de négocier des accords qui répondent à leurs besoins et à leurs intérêts. Les ententes progressives peuvent également être utilisées comme un moyen de tester les idées et les approches avant de les inclure dans un traité global. En résumé, les ententes progressives sont un outil important pour les Premières Nations qui souhaitent négocier des traités globaux, mais qui ont besoin de solutions plus rapides et plus ciblées pour répondre à leurs besoins uniques.

La gestion des déchets solides est une responsabilité partagée dans la province du Nouveau-Brunswick. Vous trouverez ci-dessous un aperçu des rôles des différents intervenants, y compris les commissions de services régionaux, dans la gestion des déchets solides :

Les commissions de services régionaux :

Le rôle des commissions de services régionaux (CSR) est de fournir des services régionaux qui soutiennent la croissance et le développement des collectivités et des régions. En ce qui concerne la gestion des déchets solides, les CSR peuvent intervenir dans la planification, la mise en œuvre et la gestion des programmes de collecte, de transport et de traitement des déchets solides dans les collectivités qu'elles desservent. Elles peuvent également travailler avec les municipalités et d'autres intervenants pour promouvoir la réduction des déchets et la gestion durable des déchets solides.

Les municipalités :

Les municipalités sont responsables de la collecte, du transport et de l'élimination des déchets solides dans les zones urbaines. Elles peuvent également mettre en œuvre des programmes de gestion des déchets solides, tels que la collecte sélective et les programmes de compostage. Les municipalités travaillent souvent avec les CSR et d'autres intervenants pour planifier et mettre en œuvre des programmes de gestion des déchets solides.

Les entreprises :

Les entreprises jouent un rôle important dans la gestion des déchets solides en réduisant les déchets qu'elles produisent et en mettant en œuvre des pratiques de gestion des déchets solides durables. Elles peuvent également travailler avec les municipalités et les CSR pour promouvoir la réduction des déchets et la gestion durable des déchets solides.

La province du Nouveau-Brunswick :

La province du Nouveau-Brunswick est responsable de la réglementation de la gestion des déchets solides dans la province. Elle peut établir des normes et des lignes directrices pour la gestion des déchets solides, ainsi que des programmes de financement pour soutenir les initiatives de gestion des déchets solides. La province peut également travailler avec les municipalités, les CSR et d'autres intervenants pour promouvoir la réduction des déchets et la gestion durable des déchets solides.

En résumé, la gestion des déchets solides est une responsabilité partagée dans la province du Nouveau-Brunswick, impliquant les commissions de services régionaux, les municipalités, les entreprises et la province elle-même. Chacun de ces intervenants joue un rôle important dans la planification, la mise en œuvre et la gestion des programmes de gestion des déchets solides dans la province.

The Competition Bureau has filed an application with the Competition Tribunal, alleging that Volkswagen Canada Inc. (“VW”) has made false or misleading representations to the public in its advertising for certain 2017 and 2018 model year vehicles. The Competition Tribunal will hear the case at a future date. The Competition Act prohibits the making of false or misleading representations to the public for the purpose of promoting products or services. VW has promoted its TDI Clean Diesel technology as a “clean diesel” that is environmentally friendly, and has also claimed that TDI Clean Diesel technology meets and exceeds the environmental standards of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). According to the Competition Bureau’s application, these claims are false or misleading because VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not actually meet or exceed the environmental standards of the EPA. The Competition Bureau alleges that VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not meet the EPA standards for nitrogen oxide emissions. The Competition Bureau also alleges that VW has made false or misleading representations in its advertising in that it has failed to disclose the presence of a device called a “defeat device” in its TDI Clean Diesel technology. A defeat device is a device that is designed to produce lower emissions of nitrogen oxides when the vehicle is being tested than during normal operation. VW has admitted that defeat devices were installed in its TDI Clean Diesel technology. The Competition Bureau’s application also alleges that VW has made false or misleading representations in its advertising by claiming that its TDI Clean Diesel technology is “clean diesel” technology that is environmentally friendly. The Competition Bureau alleges that these claims are false or misleading because VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not actually meet or exceed the environmental standards of the EPA. The Competition Bureau seeks an order from the Competition Tribunal requiring VW to cease making false or misleading representations in its advertising, and to pay an administrative monetary penalty of up to $10 million.  The Competition Act does not provide for monetary remedies for individual consumers.

Cependant, vous pouvez trouver des monographies de produits de médicaments génériques sur le site Web de la Base de données sur les produits pharmaceutiques (BDPP). La Loi sur le droit d’auteur ne contient aucune disposition obligeant l’Office de la propriété intellectuelle du Canada à vérifier l’exactitude des déclarations du demandeur, et cela, même dans le cas d’un auteur qui se serait présenté comme tel, mais qui ne serait pas l’auteur véritable de l’œuvre. La Loi sur le droit d’auteur est une loi sur la responsabilité civile. Cela signifie que, si une personne commet une violation du droit d’auteur, la personne lésée peut intenter une action en justice pour obtenir une indemnisation. Dans le cas d’une violation du droit d’auteur, le détenteur du droit d’auteur est tenu de prouver que l’auteur présumé de l’œuvre n’est pas l’auteur véritable et qu’il n’a pas obtenu le droit d’utiliser l’œuvre ni d’en faire une copie. Si l’auteur présumé peut prouver qu’il est bien le détenteur du droit d’auteur et qu’il a obtenu la permission d’utiliser l’œuvre, il ne peut être tenu responsable d’une violation du droit d’auteur. Il est donc très important de conserver tous les documents ayant trait à une œuvre, tels que les ententes de cession ou de licence. Il est également important de noter que la Loi sur le droit d’auteur ne protège pas une idée ou un concept. Elle protège uniquement la forme d’expression d’une idée. Par exemple, si vous avez une idée de livre et que vous la racontez à quelqu’un, cette personne peut utiliser cette idée pour écrire son propre livre. Cependant, si vous avez écrit le livre et que quelqu’un d’autre le copie sans votre permission, vous pouvez intenter une action en justice pour violation du droit d’auteur. Il est important de comprendre que la Loi sur le droit d’auteur est une loi sur la responsabilité civile et que la responsabilité de vérifier l’exactitude des déclarations du demandeur incombe à la personne lésée. Si vous avez des questions ou des préoccupations concernant la Loi sur le droit d’auteur, il est recommandé de consulter un avocat ou un expert en propriété intellectuelle.

Public office holders must publicly declare their recusal in writing as soon as possible, and no later than 20 days after becoming aware of the conflict of interest. You can view public declarations of recusal on the website of the department or agency for which the public office holder works. You can also view public declarations of recusal for ministers and parliamentary secretaries on the website of the Privy Council Office. What is a public declaration of recusal? A public declaration of recusal is a document that a reporting public office holder must publicly disclose when they have recused themselves from a decision, matter or action. This requirement ensures that the reporting public office holder’s recusal is known to Canadians. A public declaration of recusal is a report on the website of the department or agency for which the public office holder works, or a notice in the Canada Gazette in the case of ministers. What is a conflict of interest? A conflict of interest is a situation where a public office holder’s private interests, or those of their relatives, might improperly influence the public office holder’s decision making or actions. What is the purpose of the Conflict of Interest Act? is to minimize the possibility of conflicts of interest arising in the course of the duties and functions of a public office holder. The Act provides for a process for recusing and disclosing all assets and liabilities that could give rise to a conflict of interest. It also provides for prohibitions and restrictions on outside activities, and on accepting gifts and other benefits. What are the requirements for reporting public office holders under the Conflict of Interest Act? Reporting public office holders are required to disclose all assets and liabilities that could give rise to a conflict of interest. They are also required to recuse themselves from any decision, matter or action that could give rise to a conflict of interest. They must also comply with any prohibitions and restrictions on outside activities, and on accepting gifts and other benefits.  The Act also provides for a process for investigating and addressing allegations of breaches of the Act. What is the role of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner? is responsible for administering the Conflict of Interest Act. The Commissioner investigates allegations of breaches of the Act, and makes recommendations to the Governor in Council on how to address any breaches. The Commissioner also provides guidance and advice to public office holders on their obligations under the Act.

This means that a former spouse is not considered to be an immediate family member. Therefore, you would not be entitled to bereavement leave under the Code to attend the funeral of a former spouse. The Office of the Languages Commissioner. You can contact us if you think your rights under the Official Languages Act have been infringed upon. We offer you a service that is free, impartial, and confidential. How do you investigate a complaint? We review the complaint to determine whether it falls within our jurisdiction. If it does, we investigate and seek to resolve the complaint through facilitation or mediation. If the complaint cannot be resolved in this way, we open a formal investigation. If we find that the complaint is well-founded, we can recommend corrective measures. What happens if you find that a complaint is well-founded? We can make recommendations about measures that should be taken to remedy situations that affect an individual's language rights. We can also make recommendations about how to avoid a recurrence of the problem. What happens if a government department does not comply with the recommendations you have made? If a government department does not comply with our recommendations, we can report the matter to the Executive Council of the Northwest Territories. What happens if you find that a complaint is not well-founded? We explain our conclusion in a report to the complainant. The report also sets out the complainant's right to ask the Supreme Court of the Northwest Territories to review the case. What is the difference between a complaint to the Office of the Languages Commissioner and a lawsuit? The Office of the Languages Commissioner is an independent institution that investigates complaints and attempts to resolve them in an informal and flexible manner. The Supreme Court of the Northwest Territories is a judicial institution that settles disputes by making binding decisions. What is the difference between the services offered by the Office of the Languages Commissioner and those offered by legal aid? The Office of the Languages Commissioner investigates complaints on its own initiative or upon receipt of a complaint. It attempts to resolve complaints informally, through facilitation or mediation. It does not represent complainants or give them legal advice. Legal aid, on the other hand, provides legal services (including representation) to persons who meet certain financial criteria. What is the difference between the services offered by the Office of the Languages Commissioner and those offered by other government departments? The Office of the Languages Commissioner is independent from the government departments it investigates. It investigates complaints on its own initiative or upon receipt of a complaint.  Other government departments investigate complaints about their programs and services, and represent the government in court. What is the difference between the services offered by the Office of the Languages Commissioner and those offered by the Office of the Ombudsman? The Office of the Languages Commissioner investigates complaints about an infringement of an individual's language rights. The Office of the Ombudsman investigates complaints about decisions, acts or omissions made in the administration of a government program or service. What happens to a complaint if the department that is the subject of the complaint has already investigated it? If the department has already conducted an investigation, we can review its findings and either conclude the case or open a formal investigation if we determine that the matter has not been resolved.

- a description of the pollution prevention activities;

- pollution prevention goals for the facility;

There are limits on how much you can transfer into your FHSA in a given year. The limits are:

If the primary caregiver receives more than one CCB for the individual, you can contribute the total amount of the CCBs. The annual contribution limit is also the lesser of the annual contribution limit or the annual net income of the individual, if the individual is 18 years of age or older and is not dependent on someone for support. You cannot contribute to your FHSA if you are 30 years of age or older and have never qualified to open an RDSP. Can I make a catch-up contribution? No. You cannot make a catch-up contribution to your FHSA. Are there any limits on how much I can deposit into my FHSA in total? Yes. The total amount that you can deposit into your FHSA is limited to $40,000. The contribution room starts to build in the year an individual turns 17 years of age, up to a maximum amount of $40,000. If I have more than one RDSP, can I make contributions to more than one FHSA? Yes. If you have more than one RDSP, you can open an FHSA for each of your RDSPs. However, you can only open one FHSA for each RDSP. Can I make contributions to my own FHSA? No. You cannot contribute to your own FHSA. You can only contribute to an FHSA for someone else. You are considered to be separated when you are living apart from your partner because of a breakdown in your relationship, and you have started to maintain separate lives. The CRA considers a couple to be separated even if they are living in the same house, as long as their relationship has broken down and they are maintaining separate lives. This means that you and your partner are no longer a couple, and you are living independently from each other. You are considered to be separated even if you have not yet filed for a formal divorce or separation agreement, as long as your relationship has broken down and you are living separately. If you are living apart from your partner because of a breakdown in your relationship, and you have started to maintain separate lives, you are considered to be separated for tax purposes. This means that you can claim certain tax benefits and deductions as a single person, rather than as a couple. It is important to note that you must report your separation to the CRA in order to claim these benefits and deductions. If you do not report your separation, you may not be eligible for these benefits and deductions. If you are separated and you are claiming certain benefits and deductions, you must report your separation to the CRA as soon as possible. This will ensure that you are eligible for the benefits and deductions that you are entitled to. If you are unsure about whether you are considered to be separated for tax purposes, you should contact the CRA for more information. The CRA can help you determine whether you are considered to be separated and can provide you with information about the tax benefits and deductions that you are entitled to. Pour pouvoir étudier au Canada, il faut obtenir un permis d’études. Vous devez présenter une demande à Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC) avant votre départ pour le Canada. Pour présenter une demande, vous devez obtenir une lettre d’acceptation d’un établissement d’enseignement désigné (EED) au Canada. Pour être admissible à un permis d’études, vous devez :

- avoir été accepté par un établissement d’enseignement désigné au Canada;

- prouver que vous avez suffisamment d’argent pour payer les frais de scolarité et les frais de subsistance pour vous et vos personnes à charge, le cas échéant;

- répondre aux exigences linguistiques de l’établissement d’enseignement désigné, en fournissant les résultats d’un test de langue approuvé (IELTS, TOEFL, etc.) ou en suivant un cours de langue offert par l’établissement d’enseignement désigné;

- passer un examen médical et fournir une preuve de votre état de santé. Si vous souhaitez travailler au Canada pendant vos études, vous devez présenter une demande de permis de travail en même temps que votre demande de permis d’études. Vous pouvez travailler jusqu’à 20 heures par semaine pendant les sessions d’études et à plein temps pendant les vacances scolaires. Pour obtenir un permis d’études canadien, vous devez suivre ces étapes :

1. Obtenir une lettre d’acceptation d’un établissement d’enseignement désigné au Canada.

2. Prendre rendez-vous avec Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC) pour présenter votre demande de permis d’études.

3. Prendre rendez-vous avec un médecin pour passer un examen médical et fournir une preuve de votre état de santé.

4. Prendre rendez-vous avec un établissement de langue pour passer un test de langue approuvé (IELTS, TOEFL, etc.) ou pour suivre un cours de langue offert par l’établissement d’enseignement désigné.

5. Présenter votre demande de permis d’études à Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC) en fournissant tous les documents requis.

6. Attendre la décision d’Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC) concernant votre demande de permis d’études.

7. Si votre demande est acceptée, vous recevrez votre permis d’études et vous pourrez commencer vos études au Canada.

However, a record suspension does not prevent you from receiving a Canadian passport, or prohibit you from travelling outside Canada. How do I know if I am eligible for a record suspension? To be eligible for a record suspension under the Criminal Records Act, a specified period of time must have elapsed after the end of the sentence imposed. This is the period of good conduct. To be eligible for a record suspension, you must have been convicted under a federal Act or regulation and have been convicted in Canada, or been convicted under a federal Act or regulation and have been sentenced in Canada. You may also apply if you were convicted under an Act of the Parliament of Canada from before 1992 that was later replaced by a federal Act or regulation, and if the offence is no longer an offence under an Act of Parliament. You are not eligible if you have been convicted of a sexual offence involving a child and you are currently designated, or if you are currently serving a court-ordered sentence, including probation, conditional sentence or parole. You are also not eligible if you are convicted of an offence referred to in Schedule 1 of the Criminal Records Act. For a record suspension under the Criminal Records Act, the period during which you cannot apply is as follows:

• if you were convicted of an offence that was prosecuted summarily, you must wait one year after the completion of your sentence; • if you were convicted of an offence that was prosecuted by way of indictment, you must wait three years after the completion of your sentence. What is the application process? All applications must be sent to the Board. For the necessary forms and to obtain a list of the documentation required, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. You may wish to seek the assistance of a lawyer, a community legal clinic, or a local John Howard Society to help you fill out the application forms. You must provide complete information about the convictions and sentences you want to have pardoned. You must also provide three character references, which can be signed by people who know you personally, such as family members, neighbours, co-workers and employers. In addition to the above, you must provide the Board with the following documents:

• a certified copy of your criminal record from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Criminal Records
• a certified copy of your court record from the Clerk of the Court of Appeal or the Clerk of the
• Provincial Court in the province where you were convicted. You must also give the Board a certified copy of your driving record from the provincial or territorial department of transport that issued your driver's licence. If you have been convicted of a sexual offence involving a child, you must give the Board a certified copy of your record of non-payment of child support. Where can I get copies of my criminal record, court record and driving record? To get a certified copy of your criminal record, you must contact the RCMP Criminal Records Records and Identification Services Division at the following address:

• RCMP Criminal Records Records and Identification Services Division CPCS
P.O. Box 8786 Ottawa ON K1G 3M8

For more information, call the RCMP at 1-800-874-2652. To get a certified copy of your court record, you must contact the Clerk of the Court of Appeal or the Clerk of the Provincial Court in the province where you were convicted. For more information about where to get a certified copy of your court record, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. To get a certified copy of your driving record, you must contact the provincial or territorial department of transport that issued your driver's licence. For more information about where to get a certified copy of your driving record, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. What will the Board do with my application? The Board will review your application to make sure you are eligible and that all the necessary documentation is included. If your application is incomplete, the Board will contact you and give you time to provide the missing information. The Board may refuse to order a record suspension if the Board is not satisfied that you were of good conduct. The Board will notify you if your application has been refused and give you the reasons for the refusal. A federal business corporation is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA). A federal business corporation is a separate legal entity from the people who own and manage it. It has the same powers as an individual person and can exercise its powers in its name. A corporation can sue or be sued, it can enter into contracts and hold property, it can borrow money, it can issue shares, it can be charged with an offence, and it can hold court. In a corporation, shareholders hold ownership in the corporation through their shares. The shareholders elect a board of directors to oversee and manage the corporation. The board of directors hires the officers to manage the day-to-day business of the corporation.

The corporation is a separate legal entity from its shareholders. In other words, the shareholders, directors, and officers are not personally responsible for the corporation’s liabilities or debts. The corporation is liable for its own debts and obligations. A federal business corporation’s name must have a distinctive element, a descriptive element and a corporate suffix (for example, “Bob’s Coffee Inc.”). You do, however, need a Yukon territorial park permit to operate a commercial film production in one of its parks. This distinction is important for a number of reasons, but most importantly because operating a commercial film production in a territorial park requires additional risk management considerations that simply filming in a territorial park does not. For example, when operating a commercial film production in a territorial park, the film production company must have a Yukon territorial park permit, and the film production company must have a Yukon territorial park permit holder on site at all times. La Loi sur les brevets actuelle a été promulguée en 1970. Elle prévoit que la durée d’un brevet est de 17 ans à compter de la date de la délivrance. La Convention sur le brevet européen, que le Canada a signée en 2019, prévoit que la durée d’un brevet est de 20 ans à compter de la date de dépôt. La Convention sur le brevet européen prévoit une période de transition d’un an à compter de son entrée en vigueur, au cours de laquelle les pays signataires peuvent choisir entre le régime actuel et le régime proposé par la Convention. Au Canada, la transition se fera le 30 juin 2021. La Loi sur les brevets de 1970 prévoit également que la durée d’un brevet est de 20 ans à compter de la date de dépôt, mais seulement pour les brevets qui ont été déposés après le 30 juin 2021.

Les chiffres des charges présentés selon la comptabilité d’exercice et ceux des crédits budgétaires fédéraux sont tirés de la même source, à savoir le Système normalisé des comptes publics du Canada, mais sont calculés différemment. La comptabilité d’exercice est axée sur le moment où les charges sont engagées, tandis que les crédits budgétaires fédéraux sont axés sur le moment où les charges sont payées. L’écart entre les deux chiffres est attribuable à la comptabilisation des charges à payer, qui est une obligation de payer une somme qui n’a pas encore été payée. Les charges à payer constituent une obligation envers les fournisseurs, mais elles ne constituent pas une dépense avant d’avoir été payées. Par conséquent, les charges à payer sont exclues des charges présentées selon la comptabilité d’exercice, mais elles sont incluses dans les crédits budgétaires fédéraux. Les charges à payer comprennent les salaires, les traitements et les avantages sociaux, les services publics, les fournitures et les matériaux, et les autres charges. Les charges à payer sont généralement payées dans les 30 jours suivant la date de facturation, mais elles peuvent être payées plus tard, selon les conditions de paiement convenues avec les fournisseurs. Les crédits budgétaires fédéraux sont utilisés pour financer les dépenses du gouvernement fédéral, tandis que les charges présentées selon la comptabilité d’exercice sont utilisées pour mesurer la performance financière du gouvernement. Par conséquent, il est important de comprendre les différences entre ces deux chiffres et de les interpréter de manière appropriée.

You have to understand a little bit of the history to understand why we’re still using grants, and why we’re still using contribution agreements, and why, frankly, the distinction between the two has become so blurred that it’s become difficult to tell the difference between the two. Okay, so the first thing to understand is that under the previous government, in the 1990s, the Canada Labour Force Development Board was abolished, and the Labour Force Development Board, which is a federal-provincial board, was replaced by Human Resources Development Canada. So, HRDC was created to manage the labour force development system. In addition, the Labour Market Development Agreements were replaced by the Canada-Province Fiscal Arrangements.
